title: Define canonical performance-signature artifact and publishing workflow for model onboarding & pinning
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Current model onboarding produces a loosely structured 'performance profile' PDFs/rows with inconsistent keys, making automated pinning, rollback decisions, and billing comparisons brittle. Goal: Introduce a compact, machine- and human-readable 'performance-signature' artifact (JSON document) that captures canonical metrics, test harness metadata, input distributions, and pin-recommendations. This artifact should be the single source of truth used by the Console, release jobs, and the profile registry to enable deterministic version pinning, automated compatibility checks, and clearer customer-facing SLAs. Scope: - Define the JSON schema for the performance-signature (latency percentiles, throughput, token cost estimates, test harness commit, dataset samples, sequence-length distributions, supported quantizations). - Mapping from signature -> pin recommendation (default, conservative, cost-optimized). - Publishing workflow: verification gates, signed attestations, automated registry entry, and an API hook for Console to display signatures. - Migration plan for existing profiles and a back-compat layer for older 'profile' rows. Out of scope: runtime kernel selection logic; detailed benchmarking runner work (ENG owns harness), but we will specify required outputs from the harness.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 published in the model-onboarding Confluence and linked from the registry
Bench harness outputs map to all required schema fields and a sample artifact produced for two models (one encoder-decoder, one decoder-only)
Publishing CI job that signs and pushes the signature to the registry on successful verification is implemented and tested in staging
Console shows the signed performance-signature and the system can compute a recommended pin for a model version
Migration doc and compatibility layer created to pull existing profile rows into the new registry format
comments: 2025-01-16 — Kickoff: aligned with ENG and Design on making the signature both machine-checkable and customer-facing. Mateo volunteered to coordinate with ENG on harness outputs.

2025-01-22 — Decision: include 50th/95th/99th latency percentiles, p95 tokens/sec, median tokens-per-request, and an estimated $/1k tokens figure (derived from batch scenarios). Design will provide a compact visual for Console.

2025-01-28 — ENG review (K. Patel): recommended adding a 'test_harness_version' and 'harness_commit' fields to ensure reproducibility. Also called out the need for quantization profile tags (int8/q4/float16).
2025-01-30 — PM review (S. Müller): flagged customer impact for Dedicated customers; added a migration subsection to the playbook. Assigned ENG-1842 as dependency to extend the harness output schema.

2025-02-02 — Implementation update: first draft schema and example artifacts uploaded to Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/Performance+Signature+v1). Staging CI job (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboarding/pull/412) validates signature creation on synthetic runs.
Follow-ups: plan a review with Legal for the signing/attestation language before GA; schedule a Console UX sync to iterate the visualization prior to release-rc
